title: the database proxy forwards 127.0.0.1:5432 to the box's own Postgres
intention: A new device, the database proxy (cairn/devices/dbproxy/, answering as `database`, instance 0 on each box), listens on 127.0.0.1:5432 and runs as its own process and forwards every connection byte for byte to the box's own Postgres on its local port (5433 by default), so a cache box's processes reach their database at the one address the client dials.
why: Measured 2026-11-17 on akienlivingroom: Postgres was moved to 5433 (loopback only) so that 5432 belongs to the proxy (outline 11.3.7, one proxy per box and everything on the box talks only to it), and with no proxy built every db call there fails 'Connection refused' at 127.0.0.1:5432 (the db client dials _TCP_PORT 5432 when there is no socket, store.py _conn_args). cairn/devices/ holds no dbproxy folder.
traces_to: Outline 11.3 and 11.3.7 (the database proxy device, one instance per box); Law 6 (the proxy is the one door the box's database is reached by).
how: v0 is a forwarder and nothing else, and it is its own process (outline 2.3.2). forward.py holds a threaded TCP relay: accept on 127.0.0.1:<listen>, dial 127.0.0.1:<upstream>, pump both ways, close both when either end closes, and count connections and refusals. `python -m cairn.devices.dbproxy` runs it in the foreground; holding the listen port is its singleton, and it writes its record (pid, ports, state, counts) to ~/.cairn/devices/dbproxy/0/relay.json on start and on each connection. Ports: CAIRN_DBPROXY_LISTEN_PORT (default 5432) and CAIRN_DBPROXY_POSTGRES_PORT (default 5433). Where the listen port is already held (the home box, where Postgres itself listens on 5432) the process records state 'held' and exits 0, forwarding nothing. device.py's DatabaseProxyDevice is the face the bus wakes on `cairn database start`: if the record's pid is not alive it spawns the process detached and windowless (windowless_spawn: background_pythonw and detached_kwargs, so no console on Windows, outline 5.3.5.3.2), and state() reads the record. shim.py answers as `database`; the charter declares answers_as `database`; 0/bin/dbproxy is the self-named launcher.

clauses.claim: bytes written to the relay reach the upstream and the upstream's reply comes back, for two concurrent connections kept apart
the listener is bound to 127.0.0.1 only
when the listen port is already held (the home box), `python -m cairn.devices.dbproxy` exits 0, its record says held, and it forwards nothing
when the upstream refuses, the client's connection is closed and the record counts the refusal

the device is its own process: waking the device spawns a process whose pid is not the waker's, that listens on the listen port and writes its record; a second wake spawns nothing more; on Windows the spawn takes background_pythonw and detached_kwargs
the device answers as `database`: the shim's device_id and the charter's answers_as are both `database`

decisions.text: D1: the charter, written through the artifact door before BUILDME: component dbproxy, answers_as database, runtime_role device, owner CC.

D2: forward.py: the threaded relay (listen and upstream ports as arguments, counters, an on_change callback for the record, stop() closes the listener); __main__.py runs it in the foreground, writes relay.json, records 'held' and exits 0 on EADDRINUSE.

D3: device.py and shim.py: DatabaseProxyDevice spawns `python -m cairn.devices.dbproxy` detached and windowless when the record's pid is not alive, and reads the record for state(); DatabaseProxyShim answers as database; 0/bin/dbproxy launches like inferenceproxy's.
D4: the proof drives the relay over ephemeral ports with a fake upstream, runs the process under a scratch HOME, and wakes the device there, one tooth per clause.

out: the db client waking the proxy on a refused connection (db_domain's own ticket)

orient.request: build the database proxy device v0 at cairn/devices/dbproxy: its own process relaying 127.0.0.1:5432 to the box's Postgres port, answering as database
orient.intent: A new device dbproxy (answers as database) whose own process relays TCP from 127.0.0.1:5432 to 127.0.0.1:<Postgres port, default 5433>, records itself in instance space, exits 0 recording 'held' where 5432 is taken, and is spawned windowless by its bus face when not running.
orient.scope: IN: cairn/devices/dbproxy/ (charter, relay, process entry, device, shim, launcher, proof). OUT: the db client's wake on refused, the home-to-remote sync, owner gates, the published client tool, every other component.

constraints.text: 2.3.2 An internal device is its own process.
11.3.7 Every box runs its own instance of the database proxy, and everything on that box talks only to it.
the relay binds loopback only and never raises on the home box where Postgres holds 5432

out: the db client's wake on a refused connection (cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/store.py)
